scenario: A couple having a conversation over FaceTime
learner_goal: Express feelings about the partner taking texts while on FaceTime (<extra_info>Extra information: You find it disrespectful and it makes you feel unimportant.</extra_info>)
partner_goal: Justify the act of texting while on FaceTime without hurting the partner's feelings (<extra_info>Extra information: You have some urgent and important messages to respond to.</extra_info>)

transcript.speaker: Sasha Ramirez
transcript.content: Hey Hendrick, can we talk about something for a minute? When you keep texting while we're on FaceTime it comes across as disrespectful and it makes me feel unimportant. If you need to handle something, just tell me — but putting the phone away or letting me know would mean a lot.

transcript.speaker: Hendrick Heinz
transcript.content: You’re absolutely right — I’m sorry, Sasha. I didn’t mean to make you feel unimportant. I’ve been getting a couple of urgent messages about tonight’s tasting that I needed to handle quickly, and I should’ve told you instead of sneaking away. If it’s okay, I’ll finish this one short reply now and then give you my full attention, or I can put it down and talk now — whichever you’d prefer.

transcript.speaker: Sasha Ramirez
transcript.content: Thanks, Hendrick. I appreciate the apology — go ahead and finish that one quick reply, but please be quick and then give me your full attention. And honestly, next time just tell me you need to step away; that would mean a lot.

transcript.speaker: Hendrick Heinz
transcript.content: Thanks, Sasha — I really appreciate you being cool about it. There’s a vendor and my caterer sending urgent messages about tonight’s tasting and I just need to send one quick confirmation (won’t take more than 30 seconds). After that I’m all yours, and I promise next time I’ll tell you I need to step away or put my phone down instead of sneaking off. I’m sorry again — you matter to me.
